evidence.observation: The dependency path from checkout-web to payment-api to auth-gateway places auth-gateway upstream of the failed checkout payment authorization; the file records AUTH-2026-0318 on auth-gateway at 2026-03-22T14:05:00Z.
After AUTH-2026-0318 deployed at 14:05:12Z, auth-gateway reported a partner-v2 JWKS cache miss, then rejected partner-v2 tokens because only partner-v1 was allowed.
At 14:08:59Z payment-api reported auth-gateway issuer_not_allowed for issuer partner-v2, and at 14:09:04Z rejected the payment with auth_result=invalid_issuer.
checkout-web recorded a 401 from payment-api at 14:09:41Z and then reported invalid issuer while the checkout flow remained blocked.
At 14:10Z checkout-web and payment-api had elevated 401 rates of 18.7% and 21.2%, while auth-gateway had a 28.4% 401 rate and notes identifying JWKS cache miss and issuer mismatch.

excluded_red_herrings.why_not_primary: Query p95 was normal at 35 ms with zero errors, and no failed checkout transaction reached orders-db before the auth gate.
The metric notes scope the errors to static images; checkout-web reported static assets served normally, while the checkout submission failed with an upstream payment 401.
The topology describes it as vacuum-only with no schema or credential change, and the database log shows normal query latency and no errors.

recommended_next_steps: Immediately roll back AUTH-2026-0318 or correct auth-gateway allowed_issuers to include the intended partner-v2 issuer, preserving the matching JWKS namespace configuration.
Verify auth-gateway accepts a representative partner-v2 token and that JWKS lookup succeeds without fallback to partner-v1.
Verify payment-api create_payment succeeds, then run an end-to-end checkout and confirm checkout-web 401s and auth failure rates return to baseline.
Review the change validation and add a deployment check that issuer configuration, allowed issuers, and JWKS namespace agree before rollout.
